A poor scanned (image-only) PDF blocks the TutorChat enterprise deployment at every stage, culminating in failure at the go-live reliability gate:

1. **Ingestion failure**: NovaLearn's ingestion pipeline relies on standard PDF text extraction; when an image-only PDF is uploaded, the parser fails to detect any text layer, producing empty document models or indexes [NL-029-S05, NL-031-S04]. The KnowledgeHub struggles to extract any text without advanced OCR, resulting in failed ingestion of critical policies [NL-010-S06].

2. **Citation unavailability**: Because no text layer is indexed, TutorChat cannot find text offsets or create citation anchors [NL-021-S02, NL-018-S05]. The system either returns answers with no source citations or points the citation to the entire document (e.g., "page 1 of a 250-page PDF") rather than a specific section [NL-021-S02].

3. **Reliability gate failure**: Incomplete citations from image-only files fail the go-live validation threshold, which requires 85% citation correctness [NL-031-S04]. This directly violates TutorChat's reliability guidelines and regulatory compliance requirements [NL-021-S02].

4. **Blocked go-live and manual workarounds**: These failures halt deployment. For BrightPath Healthcare, compliance officers refuse to sign off on a general rollout, restricting them to the initial 100-user pilot instead of expanding to 6,500 employees [NL-021-S02]. The attempted workaround—manual external OCR pre-processing—imposes unacceptable delays: Northstar Financial's pilot was delayed by three weeks [NL-010-S06], and Dr. Vance's 12,000-page archive would require "at least three months of continuous labor" [NL-018-S05]. BrightPath ultimately experienced the longest onboarding time (9.5 weeks) due to manual formatting checks on scanned compliance files [NL-031-S04].
